idea: PQMagic's ML-DSA-87 needs about 125 KB of stack and the heap of the RAM image is split into regions of at most 112 KB, so the job could not be created. A static buffer can be registered as one more heap region.
change: suites/pqmagic_common/kemsig.c: KEMSIG_EXTRA_HEAP (heap_caps_add_region on a static array); suites/pqmagic_mldsa87 sets it to 143360.
note: Not a speed change: before, the task could not be allocated (rc -100), so there is no before value. After: FIPS 204 known-answer test passes on the device for the SHAKE variant, 12 of 12 fingerprints equal.

idea: SPHINCS-alpha's encoding table is a static array of 256-bit integers, 278 KB for the smallest set, and cannot exist in a RAM image. Rows need far fewer bytes than 32 per entry and are symmetric.
change: suites/pqmagic_sphincsa/pqc_suite/sphincsa_dp.c (per-row byte width, half rows, one heap block per row, built with a sliding sum); #ifdef PQC_COMPACT_DP block in third_party/pqmagic/sig/sphincs-a/std/wots.c.
checked: host fingerprint against the unchanged upstream table; device fingerprint for 128f
note: 128s: 583648 to 102249 bytes, 192f: 497408 to 128035 bytes. Host: identical keys and signatures to the upstream code with its static table for 128f/128s (SM3, SHA-2, SHAKE) and 192f. Device: 128f verified in all three hash families (18 of 18 fingerprints, 66 KB of heap for table and build rows); 128s not run; 192f failed, the table allocation ran out of heap (162 KB free against 128 KB table + 15 KB build rows + 20 KB job stack) and the run stopped at an assert. 192s, 256f and 256s need 332 KB or more even in compact form and were not attempted.
